items.title: Probation Period
items.text: The maximum probation period is 3 months. Termination during probation requires 3 days' written notice.

items.title: Work Permits
items.text: Hiring foreign nationals through EOR is possible but requires a special labor permit unless the individual is a citizen of Russia, Kazakhstan, or Armenia (EAEU).

content.markdown:
### Mandatory Employment Contract Clauses

Under the Belarus Labour Code, every employment contract must specify:

1.  **Place of Work:** The specific branch or office location.
2.  **Job Function:** Detailed description of duties and professional qualifications.
3.  **Term of Contract:** Indefinite or fixed-term (typically up to 5 years).
4.  **Remuneration:** Base salary plus any bonuses (must be in BYN locally).
5.  **Working Hours:** Standard 40-hour week applies unless otherwise agreed.
6.  **Social Insurance:** Explicit mention of the employer's obligation to pay SPF contributions.

faqs.question: Can I pay my employees in USD?
faqs.answer: Locally, salaries must be stated and paid in Belarusian Rubles (BYN). However, contracts can specify a USD peg for calculation purposes.

faqs.question: What is the notice period for termination?
faqs.answer: Standard notice is 1 month for the employer. Employees must provide 1 month notice for indefinite contracts.

faqs.question: Is 13th-month pay mandatory?
faqs.answer: No, 13th-month pay is not legally required but is common as a performance-based bonus in the tech sector.

steps.title: Data Collection
steps.description: Gathering timesheets, overtime hours, and any sickness/maternity leave certificates.

steps.title: Calculation & Approval
steps.description: Computing Gross-to-Net, calculating 34% employer SPF and 1% employee SPF. Client approves the payroll register.

steps.title: Fund Disbursement
steps.description: Transferring Net pay to employees (in BYN) and paying taxes/social funds by the 20th of the following month.

steps.title: Statutory Reporting
steps.description: Submitting Form 4-Fond and individual PU-3 reports to the Social Protection Fund.

items.title: 20th of Month Deadline
items.text: Most social security contributions (SPF) must be paid on the same day as wages, but no later than the 20th of the month.

items.title: Currency Fluctuations
items.text: If salary is pegged to USD, the BYN amount must be recalculated monthly based on the National Bank (NBRB) rate.

items.title: Paper Payslips
items.text: While electronic payslips are increasingly common, many local auditors still prefer physical or PDF payslips with a company seal for archival.

faqs.question: Does Belarus have a minimum wage?
faqs.answer: Yes, as of January 2025, the minimum monthly wage is BYN 726.

faqs.question: What is the standard work week?
faqs.answer: A standard work week is 40 hours. Overtime is capped at 120 hours per year.

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, all bonuses, commissions, and allowances are subject to standard PIT and SPF contributions.

steps.title: Gross Calculation
steps.description: Summing base salary, bonuses, and allowances for the reporting month. Minimum wage of approx 626 BYN (current) must be respected.

steps.title: PIT & SPF Deduction
steps.description: Subtracting 1% for the employee pension fund and 13% for personal income tax.

steps.title: Employer Cost Accrual
steps.description: Calculating the 34% social security fund (SPF) and accident insurance based on the gross payout.

steps.title: Bank Transfer & Filing
steps.description: Disbursing net salary via bank transfer and filing the PU-3 form for social security records.

items.title: HTP Cap
items.text: For HTP residents, social security contributions are capped based on the national average salary, offering massive savings for high-earning developers.

items.title: High Income Tax
items.text: Annual income exceeding ~220,000 BYN (approx $68,000 USD) triggers an increased 25% income tax rate on the excess.

items.title: 13th Month Salary
items.text: While not legally mandatory, a 13th-month bonus is a standard practice in the Belarusian tech sector.

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxed differently?
faqs.answer: No, bonuses are treated as regular income and are subject to the same 13% PIT and 34%+1% social security rates.

faqs.question: What happens if we pay in USD?
faqs.answer: Contracts for residents must be denominated in BYN, although many tech firms link pay internally to a USD/EUR rate with payment in BYN at the current exchange rate.

faqs.question: Is there an unemployment tax?
faqs.answer: Unemployment benefits are funded through the standard 6% social insurance portion of the SPF contribution.

items.title: Director Residency
items.text: A Belarus company must have a director. While non-residents can be directors, they require a work permit unless they are citizens of Russia, Kazakhstan, or Armenia.

items.title: HTP Residency
items.text: For IT companies, applying for High-Tech Park (HTP) residency after incorporation is essential to access zero-tax benefits.

items.title: Legal Address
items.text: Every company must have a registered legal address in non-residential premises. Using home addresses for LLCs is generally not permitted.

faqs.question: Can a foreigner own 100% of a Belarus LLC?
faqs.answer: Yes, 100% foreign ownership is permitted for LLCs (specifically known as Unitary Enterprises or LLCs with a single founder).

faqs.question: How long does registration take?
faqs.answer: The state registration itself is often done on the day of submission, but preparing documents and opening accounts typically takes 1-2 weeks.

faqs.question: Are electronic signatures available?
faqs.answer: Yes, Belarus has a robust Electronic Digital Signature (EDS) system for interacting with government agencies.

items.title: Remote Trends
items.text: Most tech workers expect hybrid or fully remote options. Offering only office-based roles may reduce the talent pool by 50%.

items.title: English Proficiency
items.text: English levels among young professionals in Minsk are generally high (B2/C1), but may vary in regional cities.

faqs.question: What is the average lead time to hire a developer?
faqs.answer: Typically 3 to 6 weeks depending on seniority and stack.

faqs.question: Are employee benefits common?
faqs.answer: Yes, private health insurance (VHI), gym memberships, and English lessons are standard in the IT sector.

faqs.question: Is relocation common within Belarus?
faqs.answer: Most talent is centered in Minsk. Relocation from regional cities like Brest or Grodno to Minsk is common.

items.title: 1C Dominance
items.text: 1C is the de-facto standard for local statutory accounting and HR record-keeping in Belarus due to local regulation compliance.

items.title: Data Localization
items.text: Belarusian law requires the primary processing of personal data of Belarusian citizens to be performed using databases located within Belarus.

items.title: Digital Records
items.text: The electronic work book (Trudovaya knizhka) is mandatory, and your HRIS should ideally support exports to the Social Fund portal.

faqs.question: Can we use overseas servers for HR data?
faqs.answer: Primary processing must happen on local servers, though secondary storage for global reporting is generally permitted if compliant with Law No. 99-Z.

faqs.question: Does 1C support English?
faqs.answer: Standard versions are in Russian. English interfaces are available through custom configurations or specifically localized modules.

faqs.question: Is self-service leave booking legal?
faqs.answer: Yes, but an official paper-based or digitally signed order (Prikaz) is still required to finalize the leave under labor law.

faqs.question: Are paper seals still required?

faqs.question: Can our accounting software be outside Belarus?
faqs.answer: Yes, but local tax authorities require data to be presented in Russian/Belarusian for audits, usually exported from a local 1C mirror.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late filing?
faqs.answer: Penalties range from flat fines (approx $50-$200) to percentage-based penalties on unpaid taxes.

items.title: Currency Controls

items.title: Audit Rights
items.text: Local authorities (State Control Committee) have broad powers to conduct inspections. Maintaining a 'Ready-for-Audit' folder is recommended.

faqs.question: Is whistleblowing mandatory?
faqs.answer: Internal whistleblower policies are recommended for transparency, though not strictly mandatory for all private LLCs.

faqs.question: How often are tax audits conducted?
faqs.answer: High-risk companies may be audited every 3 years; low-risk entities might go decades without a full on-site inspection.

faqs.question: Does Belarus follow FATF guidelines?
faqs.answer: Yes, Belarus is a member of the EAG (Eurasian Group on combating money laundering), which is a FATF-style regional body.

items.title: HTP Zero Tax Regime
items.text: Residents of the High-Tech Park are largely exempt from CIT and VAT until 2049, subject to periodic reviews.

items.title: Increased CIT 2024/25
items.text: The standard CIT rate was increased from 18% to 20% recently to boost state revenue.

items.title: Double Tax Treaties
items.text: Belarus has over 70 DTTs (Double Tax Treaties) which can reduce withholding tax on dividends and royalties.

content.markdown:
### Regional Tax Incentives

Beyond the HTP, Belarus offers incentives in several SEZs:

*   **Great Stone Industrial Park:** 0% CIT for 10 years, 0% VAT on equipment imports.
*   **Brest/Grodno SEZs:** Focused on manufacturing with reduced CIT (often 5-10% reduction).
*   **Rural Areas:** Significant tax relief for businesses established in small towns and rural settlements (Decree No. 6).

faqs.question: What is the VAT rate for digital services?
faqs.answer: The standard rate is 20%. Foreign companies selling digital services to individuals in Belarus must register for VAT (the 'Netflix Tax').

faqs.question: Are there R&D tax credits?
faqs.answer: Mostly channeled through the HTP residency rather than a standalone general credit system.

faqs.question: What is the threshold for a 'High Income' tax rate?
faqs.answer: Income exceeding BYR 350,000 per year is subject to an increased PIT rate of 25%.

faqs.question: What is the statute of limitations for commercial disputes?

faqs.question: Must contracts be notarized?

items.title: Telegram for Business
items.text: Telegram is the primary business communication tool in Belarus, often used as much as or more than email for internal comms.

content.markdown:
### Commonly Used Tools in Belarus Tech Firms

1.  **ERP/Finance:** 1C (de-facto standard).
2.  **Productivity:** Microsoft 365 (though usage is shifting to local/open-source alternatives).
3.  **Communication:** Telegram (Internal), Zoom/Google Meet (External).
4.  **DevOps:** GitLab, Docker, Kubernetes (highly popular in the Minsk tech hub).
5.  **HR:** BambooHR, Hibob, or locally developed solutions like Hurma.

faqs.question: Can we sell software directly to Belarus individuals?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you must account for 20% VAT if you exceed the registration threshold for 'Electronic Services'.

faqs.question: Are open source tools popular?
faqs.answer: Extremely. The engineering community in Belarus is highly active in the open-source ecosystem.

faqs.question: Is software development VAT exempt?
faqs.answer: For HTP residents, both the sale and export of software services are generally exempt from VAT.

faqs.question: What is the average CPM in Belarus?
